newsitem.title: PERU: Peru president's rating dips to 54.3 pct - poll.
newsitem.headline: Peru president's rating dips to 54.3 pct - poll.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori's public approval rating dipped to 54.3 percent at the beginning of September, from 60.8 percent a month before, a leading pollster said Monday.
The survey of 400 Peruvians by Analistas y Consultores also showed that 32.8 percent disapproved of Fujimori's record, while 13.0 percent held no opinion.

Fujimori has held relatively high popularity ratings since taking power in 1990 due and pollsters say this is primarily to his virtual defeat of communist guerrillas, economic reforms and strong, personalized leadership style.
However, 54 percent of those polled said they would not vote for Fujimori if there was a presidential election today, compared to 37.8 percent who would and 8.3 percent who had no opinion.
Fujimori is mulling a possible third election bid in 2000.
The poll, published in the financial daily Sintesis, had a 4.9 percent margin of error.
It also showed that 41 percent approved of Economy Minister Jorge Camet's performance, while 36.5 percent disapproved and 22.5 percent held no opinion.
